title: Four Fans Die During World Cup Celebrations Near Ángel de la Independencia
detail: Four people died during and after mass celebrations following Mexico's Round-of-16 victory over Ecuador on the night of June 30–July 1, 2026, as roughly one million fans packed Paseo de la Reforma around the Ángel de la Independencia. CDMX's Secretaría de Salud confirmed three deaths by asphyxiation from crowd entrapment — a 44-year-old man and two women (19 and 48) — found near Lancaster/Hamburgo in Colonia Juárez and at Río Neva/Reforma. A fourth victim, a man in his 20s, died in hospital after a medical emergency initially linked to possible intoxication. The Fiscalía General de Justicia (FGJ-CDMX) opened four investigation files, and Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada said her administration contacted victims' families to offer support. The tragedy prompted authorities to reinforce Civil Protection, health, and security protocols and to decentralize subsequent celebrations away from the Ángel.

title: Brugada Announces Plan to Decentralize World Cup Celebrations Away from the Ángel
detail: Ahead of the Mexico vs. Ecuador match, Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada announced a strategy to 'decentralize' the traditional post-match celebrations at the Ángel de la Independencia, setting up nearly 60 screen/transmission points along Paseo de la Reforma, the Zócalo, Avenida Juárez, the Monumento a la Revolución, the Palacio de los Deportes parking area, and 'Fiestas del Fútbol' across the 16 alcaldías, plus free concerts to keep fans from converging on the Ángel once it reached capacity. The plan took on added urgency after the fatal crowd crush of June 30–July 1, with Brugada reaffirming decentralization and a 25,000-person cap at the Ángel for subsequent matches.
